name: street-tenor-horn-stabs
style: Late-1990s New York boom-bap countdown rap, 90 BPM, unhurried. The scene: a cold block after midnight in 1997, breath steaming under one streetlight, tense and sly. A short dark loop of muted horns and minor strings, chopped off an old record, that hits one sharp stab on every number; heavy dusty kick, cracking snare, loosely swung hats, low bass, vinyl crackle. Lead: young male tenor rapper, high and a little nasal with grit at the edges, a confident street-corner bark, punchy and locked to the beat but never rushed; he calls each number by itself, takes a breath, then raps the line. Between rules the DJ cuts in with quick record-scratch fills, no words. The last line sits alone over bare drums.
exclude: singing, melodic hook, choir, autotune, trap hi-hats, 808 slides, EDM drop, double-time flow, female vocals, crowd chant
lyrics:
[Intro: horn-and-strings stab, kick and snare drop in, cold and sly]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Turntable scratch fill, no words]

[Verse: punchy, deliberate, one bar per line; number on its own beat, breath, then the line]
Rule number Uno: never say how much you made,
doesn't matter anyway, since the gold went away.

[Turntable scratch fill, no words]

[horn stab on the number]
Number two: never show 'em your next move,
cut the rate for the banks, hike it when you land.

[Turntable scratch fill, no words]

[horn stab on the number]
Number three: never trust nobody with the press,
before Bernie gets made off face loss.

[Turntable scratch fill, no words]

[horn stab on the number]
Number four: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Turntable scratch fill, no words]

[horn stab on the number]
Number five: never print where you sleep,
never let them owe the oats you reap.

[Turntable scratch fill, no words]

[horn stab on the number]
Number six: no credit? Forget it,
let the junkie know you better forget that.

[Turntable scratch fill, no words]

[horn stab, lower and quieter]
Seven, and nobody says it out loud:
keep your money and your assets apart, not in one crowd.

[Turntable scratch fill, no words]

[horn stab on the number]
Number eight: hold none of it yourself,
debase 'em till the numbers go through.

[Turntable scratch fill, no words]

[horn stab, sly]
Nine's the one they'd rather you skipped:
keep the auditors out, sporadic trips and you out.

[Turntable scratch fill, no words]

[horn stab, hardest hit]
Number ten: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout in stride and they ain't paid it all.

[Outro: everything drops out but kick and snare; spoken plain, alone]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.

[End]
